svg.title: AsyncPP host view
svg.desc: Fully asynchronous PP as implemented: what runs where, and when (schematic)
svg.text: Fully asynchronous PP as implemented: what runs where, and when (schematic)
The host runs about 1.7 forwards ahead of its GPU and builds the next micro-batches while the GPU computes. A stage issues j's load-back when it
builds j, but the copy waits on the GPU for forward j−1, so it still starts right before forward j.
MB4 load-back: issued at build, copy waits for forward MB3 (fence)
Zoom: PP2 while the GPU runs MB3 (same model, 2.3× wider)
① admit MB4 → load-back MB4 enqueued on the host (H2D stream waits for the forward stream)
② copy runs only after forward MB3 ends, ≈270 ms later; forward MB4 waits on it per layer (whole load if a KDA-state copy-on-write is in the batch)
push MB3 → PP3 + flag; early KV send MB3
Host builds MB5 while forward MB3 runs: host ≈1.7 forwards ahead (measured lead 1.7–2.0, bounded by the 1,024-kernel launch queue).
Host per round, long forwards (PP1–PP7 mean, measured): CPU work ≈ 65 ms (admission 16, build 5, launch ≈ 38, post-process 7); the rest is waiting.
Not drawn: the CE gate thread host-waits forward j and the downstream free flag before it enqueues the push; the transfer worker sends KV.
host CPU work (build + admit, launch, post-process)
host waits: upstream message or send credit
host waits for its own GPU (launch queue full)
GPU idle because the host is late
GPU idle: waits for upstream input
prefix KV load-back, host → GPU (H2D kernel)
load-back of that micro-batch issued on the host
next stage's forward waits on the flag (GPU-side)
early KV send to decode (RDMA, after the forward)
control messages of MB4 (sent at the end of a round)
